Show and change the settings.

wdx help settings explains every setting.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`wdx setting get`](#wdx-setting-get) | Show one setting |
| [`wdx setting list`](#wdx-setting-list) | List every setting with its value |
| [`wdx setting set`](#wdx-setting-set) | Change a setting and apply it at once |
| [`wdx setting write`](#wdx-setting-write) | Write the config file anew, listing every setting of this version |

## wdx setting get

Show one setting.

```sh
wdx setting get --name <key> [flags]
```

Show one setting

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--name <key>` |  | key of the setting, such as log.level |

- `--name` is required

### Examples

```sh
# Show one setting
wdx setting get --name log.level
```

### Output

The setting's value, default, description and where the value comes from. With `--json`: {"setting": {"key": ..., "value": ..., "default": ..., "description": ..., "from": ..., "choices": ..., "editable": ...}}

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx setting list

List every setting with its value.

```sh
wdx setting list [flags]
```

List every setting with its value

### Examples

```sh
# List the settings
wdx setting list
```

### Output

Each setting's key, value and where the value comes from. With `--json`: {"settings": [{"key": ..., "value": ..., "default": ..., "description": ..., "from": ..., "choices": ..., "editable": ...}, ...]}

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx setting set

Change a setting and apply it at once.

```sh
wdx setting set --name <key> --value <value> [flags]
```

The value is checked, saved in the config file, then applied: the daemon reads the file again, and every later command reads it anyway. Terminals already running keep their shell and history limit, and a running TIDE its colors. The file is written anew, as by wdx setting write, so comments of your own are not kept.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--name <key>` |  | key of the setting, such as log.level |
| `--value <value>` |  | the new value |

- `--name` is required
- `--value` is required

### Examples

```sh
# Log in more detail
wdx setting set --name log.level --value debug

# Follow the dev releases
wdx setting set --name update.channel --value dev
```

### Output

The setting, and what the daemon did with it: applied, not\_running (it reads the value when it starts) or not\_applied (saved, with a warning on stderr to restart it). With `--json`: {"result": ..., "setting": {...}, "reload": ..., "dropped\_settings": [...]}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `updated` or `unchanged`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx setting write

Write the config file anew, listing every setting of this version.

```sh
wdx setting write [--to <path>] [flags]
```

Each setting is listed with its description: the values set are kept as written, the others are commented with their defaults. Keys no setting has are moved, commented, to the end of the file. Comments of your own are not kept. wdx update does the same with the settings of the release it installs.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--to <path>` |  | write it to path instead of the config file |

### Examples

```sh
# Add the settings of this version to the config file
wdx setting write

# Write the result to another file, leaving the config file alone
wdx setting write --to /tmp/config.yaml
```

### Output

The file written, the settings it lists that the file did not and the keys moved to its end. With `--json`: {"result": ..., "settings": {"path": ..., "added": [...], "dropped": [...]}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `unchanged` or `written`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |
